review_comments.body: 💡 Edge Case: NaN/Inf sampling values crash request marshalling with log.Fatal `strconv.ParseFloat` accepts `nan`, `inf` and `+Inf`, and also returns ±Inf with a range error for values like `1e999`. Here err is nil for the first three, so `--temperature nan`, `--top_p inf` or `TGPT_TEMPERATURE=inf` produce a non-nil NaN/Inf pointer. `json.Marshal` can't encode those (`UnsupportedValueError`), so every provider that uses `SamplingOptions` exits through `log.Fatal("Failed to build user request")`, and that message doesn't say which value caused it. The doc comment says a non-numeric value stays nil, so these should be treated the same way: reject non-finite results in `parseSampling`. **Treat non-finite values as unset (needs import "math").:** ```` func parseSampling(value string) *float64 { v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(value, 64) if err != nil || math.IsNaN(v) || math.IsInf(v, 0) { return nil } return &v } ```` ✅ Fixed by `@aandrew-me` via Gitar Reply for a change | Was this helpful? Code Review 👍 Approved with suggestions 0 closed / 1 findings 🟡 Medium risk · Propagating user-supplied temperature and top\_p across chat-completion providers could change generated responses or cause providers to reject unsupported sampling settings. Sends `--temperature` and `--top_p` (and `TGPT_TEMPERATURE` / `TGPT_TOP_P`) in chat-completions request bodies for OpenAI-style providers, which were silently dropped in f2a5c8e. Values are only included when the user sets them, so default request bodies are unchanged. One open minor issue: `strconv.ParseFloat` accepts `nan`, `inf` and out-of-range values like `1e999`, producing non-finite pointers that `json.Marshal` rejects, causing a `log.Fatal` with an unhelpful message. Non-finite results in `parseSampling` in `src/structs/structs.go` should be treated as unset, as non-numeric values already are.
